You’ll partner with Procurement, Vendor Management, Payments, and Accounting to resolve issues and keep payments on track. You’ll also lead cross-functional automation and process improvement projects to reduce manual work, improve invoice accuracy, shorten processing times, and make it easier for teams to track invoices and queries. Own supplier and internal AP queries from intake through resolution. Investigate invoice discrepancies, holds, potential duplicates, approval delays, and payment-status questions. Keep stakeholders informed and follow up until each issue is resolved. Monitor aging invoices and backlogs. Escalate invoices at risk of missing payment deadlines and coordinate with Procurement, Vendor Management, and Payments to resolve issues. Partner with cross-functional teams to resolve issues and support accounting and operational activities. Lead cross-functional automation and process improvement projects that reduce manual work, improve invoice processing accuracy and turnaround times, and give teams better visibility into invoice and query status. Keep invoice processing and AP query workflows and standard operating procedures (SOPs) up to date. Document changes and communicate them to the teams that use them. Who you are You understand the end-to-end procure-to-pay process and have hands-on experience processing a high volume of supplier invoices in Oracle or a comparable ERP. You manage competing deadlines and invoice backlogs without sacrificing accuracy, and you’ve owned supplier and internal AP queries from intake through resolution. You bring a strong accounting foundation, including general ledger processes, the chart of accounts, account coding, reconciliations, and month-end close. You exercise sound judgment and discretion, apply internal controls and compliance policies consistently, and know when to escalate an issue. You work independently in a fast-changing environment, communicate clearly in writing and in conversation, and collaborate effectively across teams. You take a hands-on approach to solving problems, can lead automation and process improvement projects, and keep standard operating procedures up to date as workflows change. Minimum requirements 6–8 years of relevant accounts payable experience, preferably at a large multinational or global company, with hands-on experience processing high volumes of supplier invoices and resolving AP queries. Strong understanding of accounting concepts, including accruals, prepayments, and the chart of accounts. Proficiency in Excel or Google Sheets, with experience analyzing large datasets to investigate discrepancies and make sound decisions. Strong written and verbal communication skills and the ability to stay organized while managing competing priorities. Demonstrated ability to partner with cross-functional teams and follow issues through to resolution. Ability to work independently, take initiative, and deliver accurate results with minimal supervision. A proactive, detail-oriented approach to solving problems and improving processes. You will also likely have (not required): Experience working at a high-growth technology or financial services company Experience with Oracle, Zip, or similar enterprise resource planning (ERP), accounting, or procurement systems. knowledge on India TDS/GST/e-invoicing would be an add on.

title: Emergency Response Manager, APAC
description: Airbnb was born in 2007 when two hosts welcomed three guests to their San Francisco home, and has since grown to over 5 million hosts who have welcomed over 2 billion guest arrivals in almost every country across the globe. Every day, hosts offer unique stays and experiences that make it possible for guests to connect with communities in a more authentic way. The Community You Will Join: This position is employed by Airbnb Inc., however the role will provide direct support to Airbnb.org, an independent 501(c)(3) nonprofit that focuses on emergency response and provides temporary housing for people in times of crisis. Airbnb.org is governed by an independent Board of Directors and its mission is to provide emergency housing in times of crisis. From Australia to France, hosts have offered to open up their homes and helped provide accommodations to over 250,000 people. Our goal is to exponentially increase Airbnb.org’s reach and impact over the next three years. Learn more at Airbnb.org. The Difference You Will Make: You will manage Airbnb.org’s emergency responses in the APAC region but will also be expected to support responses globally as required. You will monitor disasters around the world, decide with your manager when an event meets our activation criteria, stand the response up, and manage it through to close-out. You will do this work with partners on the ground. Local nonprofits and agencies find displaced people, confirm eligibility, and provide case management. Your job is to make sure those partners are ready before an event, and that during one they have the housing supply, the guidance, and the answers they need. Speed matters, and so does the quality of the placement. You will run several responses at the same time, in different countries and at different stages. You will keep internal teams and external partners informed before they have to ask. You will work across Operations, Strategic Partnerships, Marketing, Communications, Legal, Finance, and Product to deliver one coordinated response. Reporting to the Senior Lead of Global Emergency Response, this position requires a background in humanitarian and disaster response operations, strong leadership, and expertise in building effective partnerships with nonprofits and government agencies. Experience in Social Impact for tech companies is a big plus. Much of the work is not defined in advance. You will need to set direction yourself, decide with incomplete information, and move things toward clarity and action. You must also be able to deploy to the field on short notice to manage disaster response programs on the ground if needed. A Typical Day: Monitor global disasters via news, partner alerts, government advisories, and internal signals to assess and recommend responses based on Airbnb.org criteria. Establish, activate, and oversee emergency housing responses in close collaboration with on-the-ground partners responsible for the intake and case management of individuals displaced by disasters. Oversee diverse, simultaneous disaster responses. Set priorities across them, and hold an accurate record of status, spend, and the number of people housed. Proactively communicate status, decisions, and next steps to internal and external cross-functional stakeholders and partners. Manage each response end-to-end: verify partner readiness, determine response size and stay lengths, launch operations, monitor placements, solve issues, and conclude based on clear exit criteria. Manage partnerships (including onboarding new partners and managing existing partners) during active emergencies, and ensuring smooth handoff to the Partnerships team at the conclusion of emergency responses. Promptly answer partner questions during live responses, escalating unresolved ones. Work closely with the Partnerships team to build and manage partnerships with organizations that vet and support guests, while working with our Operations team to optimize housing supply, reduce costs, and maximize positive impact for those affected. Collaborate with the Strategic Partnerships team to unify efforts and amplify our reach in response to major disasters. Enhance operational readiness during non-crisis periods. Sharpen activation criteria and playbooks, pre-position partner agreements, expand 24/7 global coverage, increase team capacity, and advocate for the product features the operation needs. Integrate best practices from experts and agencies, and cultivate relationships with government bodies and emergency management authorities in key regions before an event happens. Deploy to disaster zones on short notice to manage ground operations, and hand over cleanly when you leave. Write the after-action review for each response, and make sure the changes it calls for actually happen. Your Expertise: Min 8-16 years of experience in US / APAC or International emergency and disaster response operations, with a focus on managing large-scale programs. Direct experience activating and running disaster responses end to end. Experience working in Social Impact at tech companies is a big plus. Strong track record of building and maintaining partnerships with nonprofits, government agencies, and key stakeholders. Clear, timely, and proactive communication with internal and external cross-functional stakeholders and partners, in writing and in person. A proactive self-starter. You take initiative, move work toward clarity and action with limited direction, and you are comfortable with ambiguity. Proven ability to manage multiple work streams at the same time in a matrixed organization. Strong execution skills for delivering on organizational goals. Excellent leadership and communication skills, with the ability to influence across functions and teams you do not manage. Adaptability, and the ability to make sound decisions at speed in fast-paced, high-pressure environments. Willingness to travel on short notice for up to 30-50% of the year, with the ability to remain flexible regarding the length of stays. We believe diverse ideas foster innovation and engagement, and allow us to attract creatively-led people, and to develop the best products, services and solutions. title: Cluster Head - Security & Investigation
description:

Being part of Meesho's Fulfillment and Experience (F&E) team, will zip you to the cockpit of our
ever-burgeoning rocketship. And, you’ll shape the experience of Bharat’s next billion e-commerce users.

come with diverse skill sets and responsibilities ranging from running operations/support to managing
the supply chain, and maintaining analytics.

cities of India. Our team’s role in this ambitious mission is to reimagine logistics from the ground up
completely. This means a host of "zero-to-one" projects (takers, anyone?) to build a supply chain that

Security incidents and identifying, reducing and resolving malicious losses and frauds on the ground.
You’ll achieve it by forging strong collaborations with the Business and Operations teams, Operations
partners and Sellers alike.
You’ll work closely with the mentioned teams in order to serve our users better. To this end, you’ll also
lead key initiatives, audits, formulating and implementing SOPs and deliver impactful projects to cater to
security and loss prevention needs for the organization.

and integrity supply chain, while keeping customer experience at max”. You’ll answer this question every
day through owning the Security and Investigations charter for the Fulfillment and Experience, and
Meesho at large. What You Will Do Develop and Lead the Cluster Security and Investigations Charter for a Region comprising multiple states. ● Coordinate with stakeholders from Operations and Central Control tower, Legal, Trust & Safety and other relevant teams to design short and long-term security, loss and fraud identification and prevention strategies. ● Partner with Cluster and Area operations teams to mitigate risk of theft, fraud and other high impact incidents. ● Performing risk assessment of site & operation model and frame mitigation measures. ● Regularly do security analysis, and work with Central teams for setting the right SOPs across nodes. ● Conduct regular security and process audits on the ground based on central data inputs ● Close the audit exercise by ensuring corrective measures and action on the identified stakeholders (employees/delivery personnel/sellers/ops vendors). ● Create Org and liaisoning muscle to intervene in case of ops disruptions and untoward incidents happening in different parts of the region. What You Will Need 8-12 years of work experience with substantial experience in managing a geographically dispersed security, investigations and loss prevention team, with KRs around detection and prevention of security and loss incidents. ● Experience in Physical security operations and Investigations, preferably in E-commerce, Fulfillment, 3P Logistics, Supply chain, Operations, or relevant security experience in similar high growth tech startups. ● Outstanding organizational skills. ● Superior problem-solving and incident and case management skills. ● Experience in team building, managing, and coaching will be a plus. ● Knowledge & experience of laws applying to police & legal action and the judicial process. ● Ability to travel, sometimes at a short notice

title: Kirana Club : Product Manager II - Commerce
description:
About the role
You will own critical retailer-commerce journeys on Kirana Club, from product discovery and decision-making to checkout and repeat purchase. Your first and most important mandate will be to improve retailer activation—moving retailers from their first to fourth delivered order. This is an ambiguous, cross-functional problem spanning product experience, assortment, pricing, trust, fulfilment and user behaviour. You will be expected to identify where the real constraint lies, determine what product should solve, and build solutions that materially improve the business outcome. What you'll do Own the product roadmap for retailer activation, with an immediate focus on first-order conversion and progression from the first to fourth delivered order. Diagnose funnel and behavioural problems through data, user research and market visits rather than starting with predetermined features. Build and test solutions across discovery, product comprehension, cart, checkout, assisted buying, post-order and repeat journeys. Work closely with Growth, Design, Engineering, Data, Supply and Fulfilment, while distinguishing product problems from pricing, assortment and operational problems. Define success metrics, make clear product trade-offs and measure impact on delivered orders and repeat behaviour—not only clicks or feature adoption. Build scalable product systems rather than relying primarily on notifications, discounts or manual interventions. What we're looking for 6–9 years of total experience, including at least 4–6 years in product management, preferably in consumer commerce, marketplaces, fintech, quick commerce or another transactional product. Has independently owned a meaningful conversion, activation, retention, monetisation or transactional-funnel metric. Strong first-principles problem solver who can structure an ambiguous problem before jumping to solutions. Comfortable combining behavioural data, qualitative research and commercial understanding. Has built or materially improved a zero-to-one consumer journey, not only optimised an established feature backlog. Strong execution in a resource-constrained environment and comfortable working directly with business and operating teams. AI-native in research, analysis, prototyping and day-to-day product execution.

tokens. Producing code is cheap now, so what we hire for is judgment, verification, specification and taste. One hard rule: you
own every line you ship, whether you typed it or not. "The model wrote it" is not an explanation in code review, in a
postmortem, or in a design discussion.
About the role
This is a backend-leaning fullstack role, and a high-volume learning one. You'll build and ship features end to end — from the
data model through the API to the screen someone actually uses — writing a lot of code and getting a lot of reviews. You'll be
trusted with production early and work on real problems from your first week. The goal for your first year is simple: to become
someone the team can hand an ambiguous problem to. What You'll Do • Build and ship well-scoped features end to end, including the data model, the API, and the interface that consumes it. • Deploy to production several times a week, starting with small changes and growing into larger ones. • Debug production issues by reading logs, traces and stack traces, and get to the root cause rather than to a workaround. • Build the frontend for the features you own — clean, usable, with the loading, empty and error states actually handled rather than left for later. • Write tests that would genuinely catch the bug you're worried about. • Participate in code review on both sides: have your work critiqued, and learn to critique others'. • Ask questions early and often. Being stuck quietly for a day is the only real mistake here. What We're Looking For • At least 1 year of full-time experience. • Strong fundamentals in at least one programming language. Framework experience is not a filter — we hire for the ability to pick things up, and most people are productive in an unfamiliar part of this stack within a few weeks.

title: Senior Software Engineer - Data Infrastructure
description:
THE ROLE

Sarvam's products produce events, model traces, evals and billing data, and need to read that data back. The Data Platform team builds and runs the central data infrastructure every product uses: ingestion, streaming, the analytical warehouse, transformations, access control and audit.

We are hiring a Software Engineer / Senior Software Engineer (2–5 years of experience) to own this platform end to end. You will design, build and run systems that other teams depend on in production, and make real decisions on database internals, streaming and platform design. Stack: Go/Python, ClickHouse Cloud, Kafka, Avro, Airflow, dbt, Kubernetes, Terraform, AWS.



WHAT YOU'LL OWN & DO

 - Build and run the ingestion path: the service every product sends events to, Kafka behind it, and the pipes that land data in ClickHouse within seconds. Own schema validation, rate limits, dead-letter handling and the client SDKs.

 - Own the warehouse: ClickHouse Cloud. Design tables for the read path (sorting keys, partitions, materialized views, TTL), separate compute per workload, set per-user limits and per-tenant isolation, and attribute cost to the team that spent it.

 - Build reliable data pipelines and solve data problems: dbt models and Airflow DAGs with the BI engineers, CDC from product databases, sync and backfill jobs that are safe to re-run, and the data problems product teams bring you, such as a late source, a number that doesn't match or a query that has slowed down.

 - Make the platform self-serve: a registry of every dataset with its owner, schema, freshness and access; provisioning and permissions as code.

 - Run it in production: everything as Terraform and Helm with metrics, traces and alerts; be on call; handle incidents end to end, write the RCA and fix the root cause.

 - Grow the platform: new products keep arriving. You will help decide what the platform should do next and build it, whether that is a new source or sink, or a new way for teams to use the data.


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - 2–5 years of experience building, shipping and running large-scale, data-intensive systems in production, ideally at a startup where you owned things and were on call for them.

 - Deep expertise in at least one of: an OLAP database (ClickHouse preferred; Druid, BigQuery or Redshift also fine) or Kafka / event streaming. You understand how a columnar store writes, merges and scans data, or how a partitioned log gives ordering and delivery guarantees.

 - Experience with large-scale messaging systems like Kafka or RabbitMQ: partitions, consumer groups, delivery guarantees, backpressure.

 - Good at Go, or good at Python.

 - You know the usual data-system problems: schema evolution, idempotency, backpressure, partitioning, retention and TTL, CDC.

 - You have built or run at least one of: an event pipeline, a transformation layer (dbt, Spark or SQL on Airflow), a provisioning or control-plane service, or a multi-tenant data service with access control.

 - Comfortable with AWS, Kubernetes and Terraform in production.

 - You test before shipping, debug with metrics and traces, write RCAs, and document what you build.

 - Passion for data infrastructure and for enabling others by making their data easier to access.


NICE TO HAVE

 - ClickHouse in production: MergeTree, materialized views, projections, quotas, settings profiles, row policies, ClickHouse Cloud.

 - Kafka in depth: MSK, Kafka Connect, schema registry (Glue or Confluent), Avro.

 - dbt and Airflow at scale.

title: Product  Ops Intern
description:
WHO ARE WE?

At Composio, we are building infrastructure that allows agents to communicate with the tools you use for work including Github, Gmail, Notion, Salesforce, etc. We are a small team of engineers wrangling problems from context to search, that help us provide the most capable bridge between your agents and your tools.

We raised a $25M Series A from Lightspeed https://lsvp.com/stories/investing-in-composio-building-the-backbone-of-ai-agent-intelligence/ with some incredible angels like Guillermo Rauch (CEO of Vercel), Dharmesh Shah (CTO of Hubspot), Gokul Rajaram. Beginning of this year we 3x our ARR, our customer range from your friends in the YC batch to Wabi, Glean, Zoom and many more.



WHAT WILL YOU DO?

Building Agents

 - Write down the manual playbook as you run it, then work out what a person should never have to touch again

 - Build AI agents that watch inboxes, send the follow-ups, and keep the tracker current on their own

 - Turn repetitive outreach and tracking into workflows that keep running without you in the loop

 - Multiply yourself, so one person can keep hundreds of apps moving at once without anything slipping

   Operations

 - Shepherd new app connectors from first request to live: securing OAuth approvals and API access, spinning up sandbox credentials and test accounts, and clearing whatever verification or paperwork stands in the way

 - Hold hundreds of apps in view at once, each parked at a different stage of approval

 - Chase approvals until they actually land, not until the first email goes unanswered

 - Make the demo videos and scope-mapping docs that move partners from maybe to yes

 - Own the status of every app, so engineering, product, and partners never have to ask where things stand





WHAT ARE WE LOOKING FOR?

 - You already build with AI every day. It's part of how you work, not a box you'd tick out of curiosity

 - You stay with a problem until it's actually solved, sending the fifth follow-up long after most people quit at the first

 - You can keep fifty-plus threads in motion at once without letting one slip through

 - You work well without a map: you find the real problem before anyone hands it to you, then go fix it

 - Your first instinct is to automate a task rather than do it a second time

 - Automation, agents, workflows, and  operations are the tools you use to hit a goal, not the job itself. We want someone who cares about achieving the goal, not a "whatever it takes" task executor


On the practical side:

 - An engineering background — BTech, CS, or similar — ideally with a few projects you've actually built and shipped

 - Writing clean enough to land in a partner's or customer's inbox without a second draft

 - Able to be in Bengaluru, in person, for the full 2 months (we are willing to extend the internship tenure to 6 months if more projects come in)

 - Final-year students and recent grads equally welcome, including if you're holding a full-time offer that starts later in the year
